phase: Phase 4 - Baselines (parameter-matched CNN3D + ViT3D, real trained models)
decision_rule: PASS iff both |N_DIRAC-N_CNN|/N_DIRAC and |N_DIRAC-N_VIT|/N_DIRAC are within the locked 5% tolerance (IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md Gate 4 row), verified on the real trained model objects (model/param_count.py's exact_param_count), not just Phase 0b's architecture skeletons
interpretation: Both baselines trained with their own standard MAE-style reconstruction recipe (L_recon + L_masked only — not DIRAC's L_struct/L_topology, which have no non-contrived CNN/ViT equivalent per formalization Section 9's distinction between the D_classical ablation and these independently-reasonable baselines), under a literally identical optimization budget to DIRAC-S's own full run (gate_reports/gate_3.json): same 533 real train cases, 50 epochs, 13300 steps, batch size 2, AdamW lr=1e-4, grad-clip 1.0, mask ratio 0.75 — isolating the comparison to architecture + recipe per experimental-spec Section 17. Both re-verified exact param counts on the real trained nn.Module objects (not re-derived from Phase 0b's cached skeleton numbers) and got identical values to the locked ledger (CNN 1,546,240 / ViT 1,487,144) — no architecture drift between Phase 0b's skeleton and this phase's real instantiation. Both converged cleanly: CNN loss 0.227->0.155 (0 NaN/Inf, 49.5 min training), ViT loss 0.238->0.169 (0 NaN/Inf, 37.1 min training) — both noticeably faster than DIRAC-S's own 97-minute full run, consistent with having fewer forward passes per step (2 vs DIRAC's 3) and no graph/fusion/topology branches. CNN3DBaseline.encode_hidden() and ViT3DBaseline.encode_hidden() were added this phase (mirroring ComplexEncoder's existing encode_hidden/heads split) since both previously pooled to a single (B,z_dim) vector before any external code could reconstruct a volume from it; Decoder3D and the masking utilities from model/losses.py were reused unmodified for both, since both architectures downsample 128^3->8^3 by the same 16x total factor as DIRAC's own stem despite reaching it differently (CNN: four stride-2 blocks; ViT: one stride-16 patchify). One real bug caught locally before any GPU spend: the first Decoder3D channel schedule chosen for the CNN baseline (288->144->72->36->1) failed GroupNorm's divisibility requirement at the 72->36 step (36 not divisible by 8) — caught by the local pytest suite, fixed to 288->128->64->32->1.
next: Phase 5 (probing / transfer / uncertainty / robustness / ablations) — DIRAC-S, CNN3DBaseline and ViT3DBaseline checkpoints are all now available for comparison
